svg.title: Gatekeeper
svg.desc: Gatekeeper. A hardened broker validates and sanitises requests before they reach trusted hosts. Step 1, One exposed host: The app faces the internet and holds the keys: one bad file name hands both to an attacker. Step 2, Split the roles: A keyless gatekeeper validates and sanitises each request; only it can reach the trusted host. Step 3, Stopped at the gate: Bad uploads get 400 and 413 at the gate. A breached gatekeeper has no keys and only one way onward. Step 4, The costs: An extra hop, a tier to scale, rules to maintain; unlike a valet key, it stays in the data path.

g.text: The app faces the internet and holds the keys: one bad file name hands both to an attacker.

An extra hop, a tier to scale, rules to maintain; unlike a valet key, it stays in the data path.
internal zone · no route from the internet

text.class: tiny mono b mid f-red gk-sa
tiny mono b mid f-red gk-sb

g.text: stores the record and the file
One internet-facing host does both jobs
• parses untrusted input: uploads, file names, JSON
• holds the keys to the claims DB and the documents
One parsing bug, here the file name ../../config,
and the attacker has the host, and its keys with it.
the claims DB connection string: every policy and claim
the document store key: every uploaded file
Both work until someone notices and rotates them. Keeping the
stores off the internet doesn't help: the attacker is on the app's host.
Sanitise, then forward a clean request
• decode once (URL, UTF-8), normalise, then validate
• rebuild it from the contract's fields, drop the rest
• reject a bad value; never try to repair it
• pass on the verified caller and a request ID
gatekeeper → trusted host, port 8443, mutual TLS
trusted host → claims DB and documents
anything else, including internet → trusted host
Breached, the gatekeeper still gives away nothing:
• an extra hop and more processing on every request
• another tier to scale and keep available
• rules that must follow every contract change
• no business logic: it only validates and sanitises
The app hands out a short-lived key, then leaves the data path.
A gatekeeper stays in the path, so every request is inspected.
